The first release of open[flow]: a Max for Live device that opens a Live set to
three apps, and the two of those apps that ship as apps.

Live stays the audio engine and the source of truth. Nothing here parses or
rewrites your `.als` — the device talks to the set you already have open, and the
structure it reads lives in names, colors and device data that Live already
understands.

## What to download

| | |
|---|---|
| `SessionBridge-0.1.0.zip` | **Start here.** The Max for Live device — three files that must stay in one folder. Everything else is a client of it. |
| `set-flow-0.1.0-arm64.dmg` | The session manager: the clip grid, naming, roles, color rules, the running order, the mixer and the device chain. |
| `visual-flow-0.1.0-arm64.dmg` | The VJ rig: an Ableton Link peer that renders the set from a node graph. |

Both apps are signed with a Developer ID and notarised by Apple, so they open
with a double-click. **Apple silicon only** — there is no Intel build in this
release.

## Install

1. Unzip `SessionBridge-0.1.0.zip` somewhere permanent, and keep all three files
   together. The device loads `bridge.js` and `lom.js` by name from beside
   itself, so a lone `.amxd` is broken.
2. Drag `SessionBridge.amxd` onto any track. It's an audio effect with a straight
   passthrough, so the Master track is a fine home.
3. Wait for its Status to read **Connected to Live**.
4. Open either app. Each finds the device by itself, and lights its own dot on
   the device face.

The long version, including what each file does and what every status line
means, is in [Installing](https://github.com/ryangavin/better-session-view/wiki/Installing).

## Requirements

Ableton Live 12 with Max for Live, built and tested against 12.4.3 Suite
(Max 9.1.4). macOS 13 or newer on Apple silicon.

Nothing is downloaded at runtime and the device binds `127.0.0.1` only. Only one
copy of the device can run at a time — a second instance posts a warning rather
than fighting over the port.

## Also in this release

`openflow-core`, `openflow-protocol` and `openflow-widgets` are attached as npm
tarballs. They are **not published to npm** and are not meant to be depended on
yet; they are here so the domain logic, the wire protocol and the widget library
at this version are something you can open and read. They ship as TypeScript
source.

## Not in this release

**chart[flow]**, the read-only client the band reads off a phone, has no packaged
app yet. It runs from a clone — `npm run dev:chart` — and is the one part of the
suite that binds the LAN rather than the loopback.

`bridge/src/lom.ts` has no automated coverage: it needs Live open with the device
loaded. Everything else is covered by the suite that runs on every commit.
